column1: # aes-m06-sysvar.tsv -- objc_sysvar (48): the first table whose opcode the
# LOADER is not allowed to decide.
# Format (seven tab separated columns):
#   opcode  n_intin  n_intout  n_addrin  n_addrout  intin values  comment
# as cases/aes-r1.tsv and the rounds after it, read by the same loader
# (core/cases.c).  A '+' opcode is a PRELUDE: issued before the measured
# call, never recorded.  A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER and this
# file's CRC binds every dump to it, so ANY edit -- an appended case, a
# fixed typo in a comment -- invalidates every dump already taken with it.
# This file is written ONCE.
# WHY THIS TABLE COULD NOT BE WRITTEN BEFORE 2026-09-13
# objc_sysvar is #if CONF_WITH_3D_OBJECTS (gemsuper.c:232-236), and the
# loader used to refuse any table naming it, reasoning "TOS 3.06 = AES
# 3.20".  That is true of TOS 3.06 and irrelevant here: the machines these
# dumps are taken on both report ap_version 0340, and EmuTOS' own ladder
# makes 0x0340 mean CONF_WITH_3D_OBJECTS && CONF_WITH_MENU_EXTENSION &&
# CONF_WITH_WINDOW_COLOURS && CONF_WITH_GRAF_MOUSE_EXTENSION
# (include/config.h:1345-1354).  The guard now asks the machine instead of
# assuming: the loader records that this table needs 3D objects, and the
# dumper compares that against the ap_version its own appl_init wrote,
# after appl_init and before the first case.  An AES that does not report
# 0x0340 refuses the whole table by name and runs nothing.  TASK/M06.md,
# core/cases.h (the version guard).
# VERSION DELTA: NONE FOR THIS FUNCTION
# The EmuTOS side is the 1.4 RELEASE ROM (etos512de.img); the pinned
# source references/emutos @ 1a7484aba1bfba23e2c0899e243b6d8177fe41df is
# later.  ob_sysvar and init_3d (aes/gemoblib.c) are BYTE IDENTICAL between
# VERSION_1_4 and the pinned tree, and so is the OBJC_SYSVAR arm and the
# ladder in include/config.h.  So nothing measured here is a version delta.
# OUT_LEN IS EXACTLY WHAT THE CALL WRITES
# xif copies exactly OUT_LEN words back out of an UNINITIALISED stack
# buffer (gemsuper.c:429-432, :444-445).  ob_sysvar's get arm writes BOTH
# out1 and out2 for LK3DIND, LK3DACT and AD3DVALUE, but only out1 for the
# three colour selectors (gemoblib.c:1391-1414), and its set arm and its
# two default arms write neither.  So:
#   OUT_LEN 3  get LK3DIND / LK3DACT / AD3DVALUE   int_out[0..2] all written
#   OUT_LEN 2  get INDBUTCOL / ACTBUTCOL / BACKGRCOL  int_out[2] would be
#              the TT's stack, which measures the stack and not the AES
#   OUT_LEN 1  every set, and both bad-which arms: only the return code
# What OUT_LEN does not cover stays poisoned on both machines, which is
# what keeps the two records comparable.
# ORDER MATTERS, AND THE TABLE LEAVES STATE BEHIND
# The 3D variables are file-local statics set once by init_3d
# (gemoblib.c:1327-1344).  NOTHING resets them inside a run: wm_new sweeps
# windows and locks, not these.  So section A -- which measures the
# DEFAULTS -- must come before any set, and this table has to be run on a
# freshly started AES.  It leaves indtxtmove, indcolchange, actcolchange
# and indbutcol changed when it finishes; the dumper exits immediately
# after, and the next thing the machine does is the shell.
# ONE CASE IS EXPECTED TO DIFFER FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT THE FUNCTION.
# The colour selectors refuse a colour >= gl_ws.ws_ncolors
# (gemoblib.c:1358-1372), and ws_ncolors is not the same number on the two
# machines: 16 on the TT at 4 planes, 256 on NewTOS (DEV_TAB[13], the
# Falcon truecolor pen count).  The last case asks for colour 20 on
# purpose, so that the boundary is measured rather than guessed; a
# difference there is the workstation, declared here in advance.  Every
# other colour this table names is 1 (inside both) or 32767 (outside both).
# The reset is "none": no case here creates a window, takes a lock or
# touches anything wm_new sweeps, and a reset that swept nothing would only
# add 12 unrecorded calls to the run.
!reset
# A -- the six get arms, at the defaults init_3d leaves
# int_in[2..3] are left poisoned throughout section A: ob_sysvar's get arm
# does not read in1/in2 at all (gemoblib.c:1389-1420), so a write or a read
# there would show up as a difference instead of hiding in a stated value.

column7: get LK3DIND: indtxtmove, indcolchange -- defaults 0, 1
get LK3DACT: acttxtmove, actcolchange -- defaults 1, 0
get INDBUTCOL: LWHITE(8) where the palette has more than 8 colours
get ACTBUTCOL: same default, separate variable
get BACKGRCOL: same default; fm_alert reads this one too
get AD3DVALUE: ADJ3DSTD twice, a constant, get only
get which 0, one below LK3DIND: the get default arm, 0
get which 7, one above AD3DVALUE: the same arm
get which 99, far outside: the same arm again

column1: # B -- the set arms, and what the set did
# A set answers with the return code alone, so each set is measured as a
# case with OUT_LEN 1; where the EFFECT is the point, the set is a PRELUDE
# and the case is the get that reads it back.  A setter's echo proves the
# echo; only a read-back after a non-default set proves the effect.

column7: set LK3DIND to 1,0 -- both away from the default
set it again, for the read-back
get LK3DIND after the set: 1, 0 and not 0, 1
set LK3DACT with in1 = -1: leave acttxtmove alone
get LK3DACT: acttxtmove still 1, actcolchange now 1
set INDBUTCOL to colour 1, inside every palette
set it again, for the read-back
get INDBUTCOL after the set: 1
set BACKGRCOL to 32767: past ws_ncolors on any machine, 0
get BACKGRCOL: the refused set changed nothing
set AD3DVALUE: get only, so the set default arm, 0
set which 99: the set default arm, 0
set ACTBUTCOL to colour 20: inside 256, outside 16 -- the declared difference
